title: Cyera and Oasis: Stronger Together
gist: Sequoia explains its portfolio merger of Oasis Security into Cyera as the bet that AI-era enterprise security consolidates into one layer spanning data, identity and agents: every AI agent spawns non-human identities (API keys, service accounts, OAuth tokens, agent-to-agent credentials) that legacy human-centric IAM cannot govern, and Cyera's already-built enterprise GTM engine is the distribution weapon meant to win the standardization race before rivals assemble the same stack.

themes.theme: Non-human identity as the new attack surface

insights.claim: A 2021 thesis that enterprises would soon hold far more machine identities than human ones, with almost no tooling to manage or secure them, is described as having gone from true to far more true by 2026 — this was the founding premise of Oasis Security.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Non-human identity management is a validated, expanding budget line — screen identity-security vendors and legacy IAM incumbents for exposure to the machine-identity shift.
insights.quote: enterprises were about to have far more machine identities than human ones, and almost nobody had a real way to manage or secure them
insights.locator: Three years ago, the pitch for Oasis

insights.claim: Every AI agent creates or uses non-human identities — API keys, service accounts, OAuth tokens and agent-to-agent credentials — that carry real permissions and real blast radius and behave nothing like the human identities the previous generation of identity tooling was designed around.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Agent deployment mechanically multiplies credentials, so identity-security spend should scale with agent rollout rather than headcount — a structural tailwind independent of seat-based pricing.
insights.quote: Every AI agent creates or uses non-human identities — API keys, service accounts, OAuth tokens, agent-to-agent credentials — that act with real permissions and real blast radius
insights.locator: Every AI agent creates or uses

insights.claim: AI has pushed non-human identity out of being a niche IAM subcategory and into a board-level CISO conversation.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Budget authority moving up to the board typically shortens enterprise sales cycles and raises deal size — watch for accelerating ARR growth at identity-security vendors.
insights.quote: AI drove non-human identity from a niche IAM subcategory to a board-level CISO conversation.

themes.theme: Data plus identity as the AI security stack

insights.claim: The stated framework for AI security is that it requires securing three layers at once: the data, the identities acting on it (both human and non-human), and the agents themselves.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Use the data-identity-agent triad as a checklist to judge which security vendors are point solutions versus platform candidates in AI security.
insights.locator: As AI agents started reading, writing

insights.claim: Data security and identity security are framed as two halves of a bank vault problem — data security tells you what is actually at stake, identity security tells you whether the thing touching the data is legitimate — and only together do they cover the full path an AI agent takes through a company's environment.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Implies standalone DSPM and standalone NHI vendors are both structurally incomplete, making both categories acquisition targets rather than durable independents.

insights.claim: Cyera's core product answers where an organization's sensitive data lives, who can reach it and what is really at risk, while Oasis maps every service account, API key and agent credential able to touch that data and whether it is behaving as it should.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Defines the combined product surface to benchmark competing AI-security platforms against when assessing displacement risk.
insights.locator: Cyera knows where the sensitive data is

themes.theme: Consolidation logic and the standardization land grab

insights.claim: Whoever first builds a genuinely complete AI security platform spanning data, identity and agents is argued to have a real shot at becoming the default layer enterprises standardize on as agentic AI rolls out.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: A winner-take-most framing implies further rapid M&A in security as vendors race to complete the stack before the standardization window closes.
insights.quote: Whoever builds the first genuinely complete AI security platform, spanning data, identity and agents, has a real shot at becoming the default layer enterprises standardize on as agentic AI rolls out.

insights.claim: The practical rationale given for the merger is distribution rather than technology: Cyera has assembled an enterprise go-to-market team at a scale that usually takes a startup a decade to reach, and Oasis's product can now run through that engine into accounts it would otherwise have spent years earning.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Signals that in AI-era security, enterprise distribution is the scarce asset and the main driver of acquisition premiums — value product startups on what a buyer's GTM can do with them.
insights.quote: Cyera has built one of the most powerful enterprise GTM teams, with the kind of scale that usually takes a startup a decade to reach.

insights.claim: Oasis is said to have built the category-defining company in non-human identity in under three years, going from a standing start to a product enterprises trust with agentic access at scale.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Category formation and exit timelines in AI-adjacent security are compressing to roughly three years, shortening the venture holding period assumption for the sector.
insights.quote: built the category-defining company in non-human identity in under three years, from a standing start to a product enterprises trust with agentic access at scale
insights.locator: Danny, Amit and the Oasis team

insights.claim: Talpiot and Unit 8200 alumni are credited with producing a disproportionate share of the last decade's large cybersecurity companies, with Wiz, Cyera and Oasis all founded by people who came through the IDF's Talpiot leadership program.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Founder provenance from these programs remains a usable screening signal for sourcing and underwriting cybersecurity startups.
insights.quote: Talpiot and Unit 8200 alumni have produced a disproportionate share of the last decade
